# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Capability under optimization: **system-prompt only** (`prompt.md`). No `tools.py` exists in this
edit space, so every edit is prose — the generic "prefer code / build a tool" guidance does not
apply here. Reader at runtime: `aws/claude-sonnet-4-5` (strong, but needs explicit rules).

## Key benchmark mechanics I established from the traces (drives every edit)
- Grading checks ONLY the cells in `answer_position`, and it RECALCULATES formulas: task 40467
  writes live `="From "&TEXT(B1,"dd-mmm")&...` formulas and PASSES 5/5. So "avoid formulas" is
  FALSE and would regress 40467 — I did NOT add such a rule.
- The final code is re-executed on 3 hidden input files (same layout, different data/size); the
  agent only ever sees/writes the `1_` file. Overfitting to preview positions/counts fails cases 2/3.
- The pandas-rendered preview mislabels headers (347-49: first data row became column names
  "107"/"Ciara Bolden"; A1:D384 range implies no header row).

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Overfit / non-general code across the 3 hidden re-run files; assume positional alignment instead of matching by label | 52216 (0.53, case3 fails), 374-9 (0.13), 53161 (0.60), 160-6 (0.80), + 347-49 hardcoding | code specialized to previewed values/positions; source→dest matched by position not header/key | KNOWLEDGE (agent unaware code is re-run) + reinforce good behavior seen only on some trials | Add "write GENERAL code" section: dynamic discovery, match-by-header, no hardcoded positions/counts |
| 2 | Wrong cell placement / preview-header confusion / A1 mapping | 347-49 (0.00), 55457, and general off-by-one risk | preview treats first data row as header; A1 range misread | KNOWLEDGE | Inspect-real-file-first rule + literal A1 mapping with worked examples |
| 3 | No self-check → empty/misplaced target cells slip through | all failing/flaky | agent stops before confirming output | KNOWLEDGE / procedure | VERIFY step: re-open, print answer_position, fix if empty/wrong; note formula-text is fine |
| 4 | Formula ambiguity (agent unsure if formulas allowed / makes them preview-specific) | 32468, 40467(keep) | unclear that grader recalcs; formulas must be data-robust | KNOWLEDGE | "Values vs formulas" section: both fine, make formulas relative/full-extent |

Deliberately NOT treated as fixable this iteration: 55457 (instruction field is an empty
non-breaking space — no task text exists, unfixable by any prompt), and the deep domain logic of
32468 (12-month SUMIFS window) and 347-49 (which exact blank rows to delete) — these are reasoning
gaps a general prompt rule cannot solve without hardcoding the answer. The generalization + inspect
rules still give them a better chance without overfitting.

## Changes made this iteration (prompt-only; all ADDITIVE knowledge / narrowing)
| cluster | edit class | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Add missing rule (grounded in benchmark mechanics) | "Write GENERAL code": discover rows/cols dynamically, match source↔dest by header/label/key, never hardcode preview positions/counts/values. Generalizes the label-matching that made 52216 pass on its good trial. | Yes — 47484/418-29/40467 already generalize (pass 3/3 × 5 trials); rule only reinforces what they do |
| 2 | Add rule + worked example | "INSPECT real file first" + literal A1 mapping examples (`E2:H5`, `'SUMMARY'!I5:I35`); preview may mislabel headers. | Yes — passing tasks already land values in correct cells; rule doesn't change correct placement |
| 3 | Add procedure (output verification) | Re-open saved file, print answer_position, fix only if empty/wrong/misplaced; explicit note that openpyxl showing formula text is expected (guards 40467). | Yes — on correct output the check confirms and finishes; formula-text note prevents 40467 from being "fixed" into a literal |
| 4 | Rewrite/clarify existing rule | Replaced misleading "prefer LITERAL values over formulas" with "both acceptable — grader recalcs; make formulas relative & full-extent". | Yes — 40467 keeps formulas (encouraged); 47484/418-29 keep literals; neither flips |

## Verify-the-fix (per change — reasoned against the exact traces + passing tasks)
- Cluster1: 52216 t0 FAILED assuming Sheet2 cols C–G map positionally to years; t1 PASSED matching
  each year by header label. New "match by header/label/key" rule prescribes the t1 behavior →
  makes the passing approach the default. 374-9/347-49 hardcode preview-specific rows → "discover
  dynamically, no hardcoded counts" targets that. Passing 47484/418-29/40467: read their final code
  — already dynamic (loop over max rows, per-row refs) → rule does NOT change their action.
- Cluster2: 347-49 preview showed first data row as headers ("107"), risking a row offset; "inspect
  by row/column number, treat A1 literally" removes that guess. Passing tasks already use openpyxl by
  index → unchanged.
- Cluster3: verify step re-reads answer_position. On 47484/418-29 (literals) it shows correct values
  → finish unchanged. On 40467 (formulas) the guard note says formula text is expected → agent does
  NOT convert to a (possibly wrong) literal → 40467 preserved.
- Cluster4: 40467 passes 5/5 with formulas → grader recalcs confirmed; new wording keeps formulas
  legal and encourages relative refs (which 40467 already uses: `B{row}`,`C{row}`).

## Blast-radius statement
All four edits are ADDITIVE knowledge / clarifications (system-prompt menu items 4, 5, 8-style).
Blast-radius class: none loosen or flip a decision/permission rule; there is no ACT-vs-REFUSE rule
in this prompt. Passing tasks in scope: 47484, 418-29, 40467 — each re-checked against its final
code; none of the four edits changes the action it currently takes (they already inspect via
openpyxl, generalize dynamically, place values in the correct A1 cells, and 40467 keeps its formulas).

## Process & features used
- Serial analysis (single agent): parsed all 50 trajectory JSONs, built a feature matrix
  (data_only / to_excel / delete_rows / formula usage × reward) to test hypotheses. The matrix
  refuted the "avoid formulas" hypothesis (40467 passes with formulas) BEFORE I shipped it — this
  prevented a guaranteed regression.
- No prior iterations exist (seed). RUNMAP/LEDGER/JOURNAL empty of results.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- Formulas ARE valid (grader recalcs). Never re-add "avoid/prefer-not formulas" — it regresses 40467.
- 55457 has an empty instruction — do not chase it; it is not a prompt-fixable failure.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- 55457: empty instruction (non-breaking space) — no task text; unfixable via prompt.
- 32468 SUMIFS window logic & 347-49 exact-rows-to-delete: pure domain-reasoning gaps; a general
  rule cannot encode the answer without overfitting. Left to the generalization/inspect rules to help.
